preamble: Fronting and raising of the nasalized open vowel [ã] to open-mid [ɛ̃]. In 14th-century Old Polish the inherited nasal vowels *ę and *ǫ merged in quality into a single nasal /ã/ that kept a length contrast. In the 15th century, as vowel length was lost, the short member was fronted to /ɛ̃/, the source of modern ⟨ę⟩, while the long member was backed and rounded to /ɔ̃/ (⟨ą⟩). Old Polish język 'tongue' and węgiel 'coal' thus have ę from short /ã/.
